To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the F-terms in 4 d $ \mathcal {N}=2$ theories with a non-trivial Ω-plane deformation can be mapped to the F-terms on 2d $ \mathcal N=\left ( {2,2 } \right )$ gauged linear sigma models, with a suitable choice of the superpotentials.
We have discovered a new duality relating F-terms of 2d and 4d supersymmetric field theories.
the chiral ring and the Coulomb branch geometry of the 4-dimensional theory are described, at large N and in the Ω-deformed limit, by a 2-dimensional theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of supersymmetric gauge theories in two and four dimensions.
the quantization of the Heisenberg spin chain and its relation to the Seiberg–Witten theory of 4d supersymmetric gauge theories.
the study of the Coulomb branch in the context of the 4d/2d correspondence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2d/ 4d duality is the 2d counterpart of Nekrasv’s quantization procedure for the 4d gauge theories.
the duality is a new way of understanding the AGT correspondence in the context of supersymmetric gauge theories, which is a very interesting and promising direction for future research.
we propose a new 2d/ 4d duality which is a natural refinement of the 2d/2d AGT correspondence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the duality is an example of a 2d-4d correspondence.
the 4d/2d duality is a new example of 2d/2d dualities.
the duality between two- and four-dimensional theories is a new tool for studying the integrability of the former and for understanding the structure of the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Coulomb branches of 4 d theories are in one-to-one correspondence with certain two-dimensional field theories.
2d/2d dualities are in one to one correspondence with 4d/4d dualities.
the quantization of the Heisenberg spin chain is deeply intertwined with the quantization of supersymmetric gauge theories in two and four dimensions.
